`docs/architecture/inventory.md`:

```md
# Inventory management

Staff can view and edit a player's **inventory** (41 slots: hotbar 0–8, main 9–35, boots/leggings/chestplate/helmet 36–39, offhand 40) and **Ender Chest** (27 slots) per Paper server from the player profile. Inventories are per server: every server keeps its own copy, so the dashboard selects the server first.

```
Paper plugin ──snapshot (join, quit, every 5 min, on request)──▶ backend (inventory_snapshots, revision n)
     ▲                                                              │
     │ GET pending (every 3 s)                                       │  dashboard edit (baseRevision n)
     │  ◀── revision: per-slot compare-and-set changes ─────────────┘  → inventory_revisions (PENDING)
     └── POST result: APPLIED / CONFLICT / REJECTED + fresh snapshot
```

## Edit safety

Items must never be duplicated or lost, even while the player is playing:

- **Optimistic lock.** An edit is based on the snapshot revision shown in the dashboard. If a newer snapshot arrived, the backend answers `409 STALE_REVISION` and the editor reloads.
- **One pending edit per inventory.** A second edit while one is waiting is refused (`409 PENDING_EDIT`); a pending edit can be cancelled.
- **Per-slot compare-and-set.** Every change carries the fingerprint (SHA-256 of the full serialized item) the slot must still contain. On the server, all slots are verified and all target items are built *before* any slot is touched, in a single main-thread task. If any slot changed in game, nothing is applied and the revision ends as `CONFLICT`.
- **No item data from the browser.** The dashboard never sends serialized items. Moving or editing an existing item references it by fingerprint (`base`); the backend resolves the stored item data and sends it to the server, so all components (formatting, attributes, custom data) survive. New items are created from the item ID only; the server validates material, stack size and enchantments (`REJECTED` with the reason otherwise).
- **Exactly once.** A revision that was applied but whose result could not be delivered is never applied again; the plugin re-sends the result until the backend acknowledges it.

Only the fields an editor changed are sent: name, lore and enchantments of an untouched item are kept exactly as they are. Names and lore entered in the dashboard are plain, non-italic text.

## Online and offline players

Edits for a player who is online on the selected server apply within a few seconds. Edits for offline players are queued and applied the next time the player joins **that** server; the dashboard shows the queued edit until then. "Request snapshot" asks the server for a fresh copy (only while the player is online there).

## Rollback and history

Every edit is a revision with author, reason, the changed slots and its outcome (`PENDING`, `APPLIED`, `CONFLICT`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`, `ROLLED_BACK`). Rolling back an applied revision creates a new revision with the inverse changes, again protected by compare-and-set: if the items were changed afterwards, the rollback ends as a conflict instead of overwriting newer state.

## Permissions and audit

| Permission | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `players.view.inventory` | Viewing inventories, Ender Chests and history, requesting snapshots |
| `players.edit.inventory` | Creating, cancelling and rolling back edits |

Audit actions: `inventory.edit_requested`, `inventory.rollback_requested`, `inventory.revision_cancelled`, `inventory.revision_applied`, `inventory.revision_conflict`, `inventory.revision_rejected`. Changes are pushed live to open dashboards (`inventory.changed`).

## Configuration (Paper `config.properties`)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory-sync` | `true` | Synchronise player inventories |
| `enderchest-sync` | `true` | Synchronise Ender Chests |
| `inventory-sync-interval-seconds` | `300` | Periodic snapshot interval (30–3600) |

# Architecture overview

```
 Minecraft players
        │
 ┌──────▼──────┐                         ┌────────────────────────── Docker Compose ─────────────────────────┐
 │  Velocity   │───── signed HTTPS ─────▶│  [caddy :443]* ─▶ dashboard :3000 ──/api/*──▶ backend :4000       │
 │  + plugin   │                         │                    (Next.js)                 (NestJS)              │
 └──────┬──────┘                         │                                              │        │            │
        │                                │                                         MySQL 8.4   Redis 7.4      │
 ┌──────▼──────┐                         │                                        (internal)  (internal)      │
 │ Paper + plg │────────────────────────▶└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 └─────────────┘                                                         * optional "https" profile
```

## Components

| Component | Technology | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/backend` | Node.js 22, TypeScript, NestJS 12, Prisma 7 (MariaDB driver adapter), ioredis, Zod | All business logic, authentication, RBAC, persistence, audit log, plugin API |
| `apps/dashboard` | Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Radix UI, next-intl 4 | Administration UI; same-origin `/api/*` proxy to the backend |
| `packages/shared-types` | TypeScript | Permission catalogue, default roles, locales, punishment enums – shared by backend and dashboard |
| `packages/translations` | JSON/YAML + TypeScript | Dashboard catalogues, Minecraft plugin messages, validation tooling |
| `apps/plugin-common` | Java 25 | Backend client, request signing, event buffering, config, messages (bundled into both plugins) |
| `apps/velocity-plugin` | Velocity API 4.3, Java 25 | Sessions, server switches, proxy heartbeats, periodic sync |
| `apps/paper-plugin` | Paper API 26.3, Java 25 | Server heartbeats (TPS, MSPT, memory), player game modes |

## Key decisions

1. **Single public entry point.** Only the dashboard (or Caddy) is published. Its route handler `app/api/[...path]` proxies to the backend at runtime (`BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL`), which keeps session cookies first-party and lets MySQL, Redis and the backend stay on the internal network. Plugins will use the same public URL.
2. **Business logic only in the backend.** The dashboard is a client of the REST API; permission checks in the UI are cosmetic. Every route is protected by global guards (`SessionGuard` → `PermissionsGuard`), and public routes must opt out explicitly with `@Public()`.
3. **Validation with Zod.** Request bodies and queries are validated by Zod schemas, which also generate the OpenAPI request schemas (`@ZodBody`, `@ZodQuery`).
4. **Idempotent startup.** On boot the backend synchronises the permission catalogue, default roles and bundled languages (`BootstrapService`). Customised roles are never overwritten.
5. **Migrations at container start.** The backend entrypoint runs `prisma migrate deploy` before starting. Migrations are forward-only.
6. **Never invent data.** Statistics are stored only when collected; a missing row means "not recorded" and the UI says so. Server metrics are shown only when reported.
7. **i18n from the start.** All UI strings are translation keys, typed against the English catalogue (unknown keys fail the TypeScript build).

## Request flow (dashboard)

1. Browser → `GET /api/auth/me` (same origin) → Next.js route handler → backend.
2. `SessionGuard` reads the `mnm_access` cookie, verifies the JWT (HS256, audience `mnm-dashboard`), loads the session row (revocation check) and the user's role permissions.
3. For non-GET requests the `X-MNM-CSRF: 1` header is required.
4. `PermissionsGuard` enforces `@RequirePermissions(...)`.
5. On `401` the dashboard calls `/api/auth/refresh` once (single-flight) and retries.

## Phase roadmap

See the [README](../../README.md#roadmap). Each phase ships working vertical slices.

# Player profiles

Players are identified by their Minecraft UUID. Search accepts the current name, any previously recorded name, or the UUID (dashed or undashed).

## Profile tabs

| Tab | Content | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | 3D skin, head, status, current server, playtime, connections, first join, client version/brand, game mode, name history, recent sessions | `players.view` |
| Statistics | Ranges, category values, daily charts, all-time breakdowns ([details](statistics.md)) | `players.view.statistics` |
| Inventory / Ender Chest | Planned (Phase 7) | – |
| Moderation | Active ban/mute, punish, history, revoke | `punishments.history` (+ issue/revoke permissions) |
| Connections | Connection history; IP addresses, IP summary and other accounts on the same IPs; approximate location | `players.view`; IPs `players.view.ip`; location `players.view.location` |
| Activity | Playtime in range, sessions, average session, daily playtime chart (7/30/90 days), weekday × hour heatmap | `players.view` |
| Notes | Internal staff notes | `players.notes` |

Values that were never collected (e.g. AFK time on networks without the Paper plugin) are shown as "Not collected yet", never as zero.

## Skins

- The Velocity plugin sends the player's signed `textures` game-profile property at login. The backend stores the skin texture URL and arm model.
- `GET /api/players/:uuid/skin` returns the 64×64 PNG. The backend downloads textures **only** from `textures.minecraft.net` (strict allow-list; prevents server-side request forgery through crafted profiles), with a 5 s timeout and a 64 KB limit, verifies the PNG header and dimensions, and caches textures in Redis (30 days; texture URLs are content-addressed).
- If no texture was reported (e.g. players who have not joined since the update), premium UUIDs are resolved once via Mojang's session server (cached 6 h, negative results 1 h).
- The dashboard renders heads on a canvas (face + hat layer) and the 3D preview with [skinview3d](https://github.com/bs-community/skinview3d). Browsers never contact Mojang or other third parties.

## Activity

Computed on request from recorded sessions, in the viewer's time zone (account preference, otherwise the network default). Sessions are split into 5-minute slices and assigned to local days and weekday/hour buckets, so sessions crossing midnight or DST changes are attributed correctly.

## Connections and alternate accounts

The IP summary lists the player's addresses with connection counts and first/last use. "Other accounts on these IP addresses" lists accounts that connected from at least one of them. Shared networks (households, schools, VPNs, carrier-grade NAT) are common; the dashboard labels this as a hint, not proof.

## IP geolocation (optional)

Location data is only stored when MaxMind GeoLite2 databases are configured. It is approximate by nature and is always presented as such — never as an exact location.

1. Create a free MaxMind account and download **GeoLite2-City** and **GeoLite2-ASN** (`.mmdb`).
2. Place them in `./geoip/` next to `docker-compose.yml`.
3. In `.env`:

   ```dotenv
   GEOIP_CITY_DB=/geoip/GeoLite2-City.mmdb
   GEOIP_ASN_DB=/geoip/GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb
   ```

4. `docker compose up -d`. The backend log shows `GeoIP City database loaded`. Databases are reloaded automatically when the files change (e.g. updated by MaxMind's `geoipupdate`).

Lookups happen once, when a player connects; private and special-purpose addresses are skipped. Stored fields: country, region, city, autonomous system number and organisation (shown as network / ISP).

## Privacy and retention

*Settings → Privacy* sets how long IP addresses are kept (default 180 days, or "keep forever"). An hourly maintenance job (one backend replica at a time):

- removes IP addresses and virtual hosts from connection records older than the retention period (country and network stay),
- removes IP addresses from audit log entries older than the retention period,
- deletes dashboard sessions that expired more than 30 days ago.

Blacklist punishments keep their IP address, because enforcement depends on it. Revoke the blacklist to stop storing it.

`docs/architecture/plugin-protocol.md`:

```md
# Plugin protocol

Velocity and Paper plugins talk to the backend over HTTPS JSON (`/api/plugin/v1/*`), usually through the dashboard URL (the dashboard proxies `/api`). Implementation: `apps/plugin-common` (Java) and `apps/backend/src/plugin-api` (TypeScript).

## Registration

`POST /api/plugin/v1/register` with a single-use token → `{ keyId, secret, serverId, serverName, serverType }`. The backend stores only `SHA-256(secret)`.

## Request signing

Every other request is signed:

```
signingKey = SHA-256(secret)                    (32 raw bytes)
canonical  = METHOD "\n" PATH "\n" TIMESTAMP "\n" NONCE "\n" hex(SHA-256(body))
signature  = hex(HMAC-SHA256(signingKey, canonical))
```

Headers: `X-MNM-Key-Id`, `X-MNM-Timestamp` (epoch ms), `X-MNM-Nonce` (16–64 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), `X-MNM-Signature`.

The backend rejects requests when the key is unknown or revoked, the timestamp is more than 5 minutes off, the signature does not match the exact raw body, or the nonce was already used (nonces are kept in Redis for 10 minutes → **replay protection**). Disabled servers get `403`.

A fixed test vector is asserted on both sides (`apps/backend/test/plugin.spec.ts`, `RequestSignerTest.java`) so the implementations cannot drift apart.

*Trade-off:* the HMAC key is the stored hash, so someone with read access to the database could sign requests. Database access already implies full compromise of the platform; the design ensures the secret is never transmitted after registration and captured requests cannot be replayed or altered.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Sender | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /ping` | both | Verify credentials and clock |
| `POST /heartbeat` | both | Status and metrics; Paper also sends players' game modes |
| `POST /events` | Velocity | Ordered batch (≤ 500) of `player.join`, `player.switch`, `player.brand`, `player.leave` |
| `POST /sync` | Velocity | Complete list of connected sessions; backend closes missing and opens unknown sessions |
| `POST /shutdown` | both | Marks the server offline; Velocity's open sessions are closed |

## Idempotency and ordering

- The proxy generates a random **session key** (UUID) per login. Join, switch and leave events reference it; the backend ignores a join whose key exists and a leave for an already closed session. Retried batches therefore never duplicate data (`{ applied, skipped }` in the response).
- Events carry the time they happened (`at`, epoch ms), so buffered events keep correct timestamps. Times in the future are clamped to the backend clock.
- One sender thread per plugin delivers batches strictly in order; a batch is removed from the buffer only after the backend acknowledged it. A batch rejected as invalid (`400`) is dropped and a sync is scheduled so the queue cannot block forever.

## Failure handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Backend unreachable | Exponential backoff (1 s → 60 s), events stay buffered |
| Buffer full | Oldest events dropped, full sync after reconnect |
| Proxy crash | Backend closes its sessions after 3 min without heartbeat (`StaleServerMonitor`, one replica at a time via Redis lock) |
| Server silent > 60 s | Reported as *Offline* |
| Player on two proxies | A player is online while any session is open |

`docs/architecture/punishments.md`:

```md
# Punishment system

## Types

| Type | Effect | Duration | Issued from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BAN` / `TEMP_BAN` | Login denied network-wide; online player disconnected | permanent / 1 min – 10 years | commands, dashboard |
| `BLACKLIST` | Like a permanent ban, **plus** the player's last known IP address is blocked for all accounts | permanent | dashboard |
| `MUTE` / `TEMP_MUTE` | Chat blocked on every Paper server | permanent / 1 min – 10 years | commands, dashboard |
| `KICK` | Online player disconnected once (recorded, never "active") | – | commands, dashboard |
| `WARNING` | Message to the player, kept in history | – | commands, dashboard |

Every record stores: ID, target UUID, type, reason, created/expiry timestamps, issuer (dashboard user, player or console), source (`COMMAND`, `DASHBOARD`, `CONSOLE`, `ANTICHEAT`), server, status (`ACTIVE`, `EXPIRED`, `REVOKED`) and revocation details (who, when, why). Expiry is evaluated on read; no background job is needed.

**Duplicate prevention:** a player can have at most one active ban (incl. blacklist) and one active mute (`409 ALREADY_BANNED` / `ALREADY_MUTED`). Commands carry an idempotency key, so a retried request never creates a second punishment.

**Audit:** each issue, revocation and note is written to the audit log in the same transaction.

## Enforcement architecture

```
 command / dashboard / AntiCheat ──▶ backend (single source of truth) ──▶ punishment_changes (ordered feed)
                                                                  │  poll every 3 s (cursor = id)
                              ┌───────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
                        Velocity plugin                                             Paper plugin
              local cache: bans, blacklists, mutes                        local cache: mutes
              • LoginEvent: deny from cache (no network call)             • AsyncChatEvent: block muted players
              • new ban / kick / warning / mute: act on online players
              • staff notification (networkmanager.notify)
```

- **No network round-trip on login.** Bans are checked against the in-memory cache, so a slow or unavailable backend never delays or blocks joins.
- **Outage-safe.** The cache is written to `punishments-cache.json` in the plugin folder. After a restart without backend connectivity the last known bans and mutes are still enforced. When the backend is reachable the plugin loads a fresh snapshot and continues with the feed.
- **Fast propagation.** Dashboard punishments reach every proxy within about 3 seconds. Commands apply their effect locally immediately after the backend confirms.
- **Old events are not replayed to players.** Changes older than 2 minutes (e.g. after an outage) update the cache but do not kick or message anyone.
- **Mutes are enforced on Paper**, because Velocity cannot cancel signed chat messages from modern clients.
- **Commands require the backend.** If it is unreachable, commands fail with a clear message instead of creating local-only punishments that could diverge.

Blacklist entries include an IP address, which is personal data. It is only sent to authenticated plugins (for enforcement) and shown in the dashboard only where `players.view.ip` applies.

## In-game commands (Velocity)

| Command | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `/ban <player> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.ban` |
| `/tempban <player> <duration> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.tempban` |
| `/unban <player> [reason]` | `networkmanager.command.unban` |
| `/mute <player> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.mute` |
| `/tempmute <player> <duration> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.tempmute` |
| `/unmute <player> [reason]` | `networkmanager.command.unmute` |
| `/kick <player> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.kick` |
| `/warn <player> <reason>` | `networkmanager.command.warn` |
| `/history <player>` | `networkmanager.command.history` |
| `/check <player>` | `networkmanager.command.check` |

Staff with `networkmanager.notify` receive a message for every new punishment. Durations: `30m`, `12h`, `7d`, `2w`, `1mo` (30 days), `1y` and combinations such as `1d12h`. Targets can be names (players who have joined before) or UUIDs.

Assign permissions with your proxy permission plugin (e.g. LuckPerms). Dashboard permissions are separate and listed in [security.md](security.md).

## Dashboard

- **Moderation** page: all punishments with search (player, staff member, reason, ID), type and status filters, revoke action, "New punishment" dialog.
- **Player profile**: active ban/mute badges, punish dialog, full history with revoke, and internal staff notes (`players.notes`; authors or `dashboard.manage` may delete).
- Issue permissions: `punishments.ban` (ban/tempban), `punishments.mute`, `punishments.kick`, `punishments.warn`, `punishments.blacklist`; revoke: `punishments.unban`, `punishments.unmute`; viewing history: `punishments.history`.

`docs/architecture/realtime.md`:

```md
# Realtime updates

**Decision:** Server-Sent Events (SSE) at `GET /api/events`, fanned out across backend replicas with Redis pub/sub.

**Why not WebSockets (yet):** the dashboard is the single public entry point and proxies `/api` through a Next.js route handler. Route handlers stream responses (so SSE passes through unchanged) but cannot proxy WebSocket upgrades. SSE keeps the one-port deployment, works through Caddy/nginx without extra configuration, reconnects automatically, and the dashboard only needs server → client messages. If bidirectional messaging is required later (e.g. live inventory editing), a WebSocket endpoint can be added behind the reverse proxy.

## Flow

1. A domain change (heartbeat, join, leave, server update) calls `RealtimeService.publish()`, which publishes to the Redis channel `mnm:realtime`.
2. Every backend replica subscribes and forwards events to its connected SSE clients.
3. Each event is only sent to users holding the matching permission (`servers.view`, `players.view`). Payloads contain identifiers only; the dashboard refetches details through the normal, permission-checked API.
4. Streams send a keep-alive every 25 s and re-validate the dashboard session every 60 s, closing the stream after logout, deactivation or permission loss.
5. The dashboard keeps one `EventSource` per tab (`RealtimeProvider`). `useLiveRefresh()` debounces events and keeps a slow polling fallback.

`Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` keep proxies and compression from buffering the stream.

```

`docs/architecture/security.md`:

```md
# Security model

## Dashboard authentication

| Mechanism | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Password hashing | Argon2id (m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1); minimum length 12; constant-time path for unknown users |
| Sessions | `dashboard_sessions` row per login. Access token: HS256 JWT (15 min, audience `mnm-dashboard`) in `mnm_access`. Refresh token: 48 random bytes, stored as SHA-256, rotated on every use, cookie `mnm_refresh` scoped to `/api/auth` |
| Cookies | `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` when served over HTTPS (`COOKIE_SECURE=auto`) |
| Revocation | Every request checks the session row, so logout, disabling a user, password or role changes take effect immediately |
| CSRF | All state-changing requests must send `X-MNM-CSRF: 1` (cannot be set cross-site without a CORS preflight; CORS is not enabled) in addition to `SameSite=Strict` |
| Brute force | Per-IP limits in Redis (login: 5/min, 5 min block) **and** per-account lockout after 10 failures for 15 minutes |
| 2FA | Schema fields exist (`two_factor_*`); TOTP enrolment is planned |

## Authorization

- Global guards: every route requires a session unless marked `@Public()`.
- Permissions are checked on the server (`@RequirePermissions`). Wildcards: `*` (Owner) and `namespace.*`.
- Users can only manage users/roles with a **lower priority** than their own role and can only grant permissions they hold themselves. The Owner role cannot be edited, and the last active Owner cannot be demoted or disabled.

## First-time setup

- While uninitialised, the backend prints a random one-time **setup code** to its log (or uses `SETUP_TOKEN`). Only someone with access to the server logs/environment can create the Owner.
- Completion inserts the `setup.completed` row (primary key), so concurrent or repeated initialisation fails with `409`.

## Plugin registration

- Registration tokens: 24 random bytes, stored hashed, single-use, expire after 30 minutes (configurable), consumed with a conditional update so they can never be redeemed twice.
- Redemption returns a key id + secret; only the secret's SHA-256 is stored. Request signing with replay protection for the plugin API is part of Phase 2.

## Transport & headers

- Use the `https` Compose profile (Caddy with automatic certificates) or your own TLS-terminating proxy in production.
- Helmet on the backend; `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`, strict referrer policy on the dashboard.
- **Client IPs:** the dashboard forwards only the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` hop. When the dashboard is exposed directly (no reverse proxy) a client can choose that value, so IP-based rate limits are weaker; the per-account login lockout does not depend on IPs. Put Caddy (or another proxy that overwrites `X-Forwarded-For`) in front for accurate IPs.

## Input & output handling

- All bodies and queries are validated with Zod; unknown fields are rejected on update endpoints.
- Prisma uses parameterised queries; the only raw SQL uses tagged templates.
- Error responses never contain stack traces or SQL.
- Translation catalogues are rendered as text and validated to contain no markup, `javascript:` URLs or event-handler attributes.

## Personal data

- IP addresses and approximate locations are only returned to users with `players.view.ip` / `players.view.location`; the other connection fields need `players.view`.
- IP addresses are removed after the configurable retention period (default 180 days), see [Player profiles](player-profiles.md#privacy-and-retention).
- Skins are fetched by the backend from an allow-listed host only, so dashboard users' browsers never contact third parties.

## Secrets

- Never committed: `.env` is git-ignored; `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- CI runs Gitleaks and `npm audit` on production dependencies.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

Please open a private security advisory on the GitHub repository instead of a public issue.

`docs/architecture/statistics.md`:

```md
# Statistics

## Collection (Paper plugin)

Minecraft already records detailed per-player statistics; the plugin reads them instead of tracking events itself.

| Category | Values | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Movement | walked, sprinted, crouched, swum, flown, elytra, boat, minecart, horse (cm), jumps | vanilla |
| Combat | PvP kills, mob kills, deaths, damage dealt/taken, kills per mob type | vanilla |
| Blocks | blocks mined/placed per type, totals | vanilla (`mined`, `used` for block items) |
| General | time on server, fish caught, items crafted/used | vanilla |
| General | active time, AFK time, chat messages, experience gained | plugin (stored in the player's persistent data, survives restarts) |

- **Active vs. AFK:** a player is AFK after `afk-timeout-seconds` (default 300) without moving their head, walking, interacting, building, chatting or using commands.
- **Chat messages** count only delivered messages (muted chat is not counted).
- **Experience gained** counts positive experience changes while the plugin is installed.
- **Performance:** a collection round runs every `statistics-interval-seconds` (default 300). Players are read on the main thread four per tick, so no single tick does all the work; uploads are asynchronous. Final values are also sent when a player leaves the server.
- **Data minimisation:** choose categories with `statistics-categories`, or disable collection entirely with `statistics-enabled=false`. Only non-zero values are sent.

Values are cumulative **per server** and sent as absolute numbers, so a failed upload is simply superseded by the next round.

## Storage (backend)

| Table | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `player_statistics` | Current value per player, server and key (all keys, incl. per block / mob type) |
| `player_statistic_snapshots` | Hourly history of the ~25 core statistics (one row per player, server, key and hour) |

Only changed values are written. The profile's *active playtime* and *AFK time* are updated from the plugin values (sum over servers).

## Ranges and charts

- **All time** uses the current values (sum over servers).
- **24 h / 7 d / 30 d / custom** sum the increments between hourly snapshots inside the range, starting from the last snapshot before the range. A value lower than its predecessor is treated as a counter reset (e.g. a new world), never as a negative contribution.
- If the range starts before collection began, the response is marked **partial** and the dashboard says so; earlier activity is never estimated.
- Ranges are precise to the hour. Breakdowns per block/mob type are available for all time only.
- Daily charts use the viewer's time zone.

## Dashboard

- Player profile → **Statistics** tab: range selector (24 h, 7 d, 30 d, all time, custom dates), category cards (distances in km, damage in hearts, times as durations, K/D = PvP kills per death), daily chart (blocks mined/placed, mob kills, deaths, distance walked, active time), all-time ore breakdown and most mined/placed blocks and killed mobs.
- **Statistics** page: network totals and leaderboards (active time, blocks mined/placed, kills, deaths, distance, elytra, fish, chat, jumps).
- Permission: `players.view.statistics`.

## API

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/plugin/v1/statistics` | Paper upload (signed): `{ capturedAt, players: [{ uuid, stats: { key: value } }] }`, max 50 players |
| `GET /api/players/:uuid/statistics?range=24h\|7d\|30d\|all\|custom&from&to` | Values, coverage, breakdowns |
| `GET /api/players/:uuid/statistics/series?keys=&days=` | Daily increments |
| `GET /api/statistics/overview` | Network totals |
| `GET /api/statistics/leaderboard?stat=&limit=` | Top players for one statistic |

Statistic keys are defined in `packages/shared-types/src/stats.ts`.

```

# Development

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 22 LTS and npm 12 (`npm install -g npm@12`)
- MySQL 8.4 and Redis 7 for running the backend (e.g. `docker compose up -d mysql redis` with temporary published ports, or local installations)
- JDK 25 for the plugins (Gradle is provided by the wrapper: `./gradlew build`)

npm 12 only runs install scripts for packages approved in `package.json → allowScripts` (argon2, prisma, @swc/core, …). Approve new ones with `npm install-scripts approve <pkg>`.

## Setup

```sh
npm install
npm run build:packages            # shared-types + translations
```

Backend (`apps/backend`):

```sh
export DATABASE_URL=mysql://mnm:password@localhost:3306/mnm REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 JWT_SECRET=<32+ chars> NODE_ENV=development
npx prisma migrate deploy
npm run start:dev -w @mnm/backend      # http://localhost:4000/api/docs
```

Dashboard (`apps/dashboard`):

```sh
BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL=http://localhost:4000 npm run dev -w @mnm/dashboard   # http://localhost:3000
```

## Quality gates

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint (flat config, typescript-eslint) for all workspaces |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` for all workspaces (includes translation-key checking in the dashboard) |
| `npm test` | Vitest unit tests (backend, dashboard) + translation validation |
| `npm run translations:validate` | Catalogue safety/structure checks |
| `./gradlew build` | Compile (warnings as errors in common/Velocity), JUnit tests and plugin jars |
| `E2E_DATABASE_URL=… E2E_REDIS_URL=… npx vitest run test/e2e.spec.ts` (in `apps/backend`) | End-to-end tests against an **empty, migrated** database |

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs all of the above plus migration drift detection, Docker image builds, Compose validation, Gitleaks and `npm audit`.

## Database changes

1. Edit `apps/backend/prisma/schema.prisma`.
2. `npx prisma migrate dev --name <change>` (in `apps/backend`, against a development database).
3. Commit the schema and the generated migration together. CI fails if they drift apart.

## Conventions

- English for code, comments, docs, commits and default messages.
- Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `ci:`, `refactor:`, `test:`).
- Branches: `main` (stable), `develop` (integration), `feature/*`, `fix/*`.
- Every user-facing string is a translation key in `packages/translations` – add it to **all** catalogues.
- Every administrative action writes an audit entry, inside the same transaction as the change where possible.
- Never show invented data: render "not recorded" when a value has not been collected.

`docs/installation/README.md`:

```md
# Installation

## Requirements

- Linux host (x86_64 or arm64) with Docker Engine 24+ and the Docker Compose plugin
- 2 GB RAM minimum (MySQL, Redis, backend, dashboard)
- A domain name if you want HTTPS (recommended for production)

Node.js, MySQL and Redis do **not** need to be installed on the host.

## Steps

1. **Clone the repository**

   ```sh
   git clone <repository-url> minecraft-network-manager
   cd minecraft-network-manager
   ```

2. **Create the environment file with secrets**

   ```sh
   sh infrastructure/scripts/generate-secrets.sh
   ```

   This copies `.env.example` to `.env` and fills `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `REDIS_PASSWORD` and `JWT_SECRET` with random hex values (requires `openssl`). You can also edit `.env` by hand – use only letters and digits in passwords because they are embedded in connection URLs.

3. **Start the stack**

   ```sh
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```

   The first start builds the images, initialises MySQL and applies all database migrations automatically. Check progress with `docker compose ps` – all services should become `healthy`.

4. **Get the setup code**

   ```sh
   docker compose logs backend | grep "Setup code"
   ```

   The code is regenerated on every backend start until setup is complete. Alternatively set `SETUP_TOKEN` in `.env` (min. 16 characters).

5. **Run the setup wizard** at `http://<host>:3000`:
   1. Welcome – backend, database and Redis status
   2. Database – connectivity, server version, migration status
   3. Owner account – setup code, username, email, password
   4. Network – name, description, Minecraft domain, dashboard URL, default language (English preselected), time zone, theme
   5. Velocity – generate a single-use registration token (valid 30 minutes) or skip
   6. Finish – summary

   After completion the wizard is locked; the setup endpoint returns `409`.

6. **Connect the Minecraft servers** – install the Velocity and Paper plugins: see [Minecraft plugins](minecraft-plugins.md).

## Optional: IP geolocation

To show approximate player locations, add the free MaxMind GeoLite2 databases as described in [Player profiles](../architecture/player-profiles.md#ip-geolocation-optional).

## Ports and exposure

| Service | Exposed | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dashboard | `DASHBOARD_BIND:DASHBOARD_PORT` (default `0.0.0.0:3000`) | Also proxies the API under `/api` |
| caddy (profile `https`) | 80, 443 | See [HTTPS](https.md) |
| backend | internal only | Reachable through the dashboard at `/api` |
| mysql, redis | internal only | Never published by default |

API documentation (OpenAPI) is available at `http://<host>:3000/api/docs` unless `API_DOCS_ENABLED=false`.

## Troubleshooting

- `docker compose logs backend` – startup, migrations and setup code.
- Backend `unhealthy`: check that MySQL is healthy and that `.env` passwords contain no special characters.
- Dashboard shows "The backend could not be reached": the backend container is not healthy yet.

More: [Production deployment](deployment.md) · [Updating](updating.md) · [Backup & restore](backup-restore.md) · [HTTPS](https.md)

`docs/installation/backup-restore.md`:

```md
# Backup & restore

> **Status:** these are documented manual procedures for v0.1.0. They have **not yet been verified end-to-end** in CI; automated, scheduled backups with retention and tested restore are planned for the production-readiness phase.

All persistent state lives in two Docker volumes:

| Volume | Contents | Critical |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `minecraft-network-manager_mysql-data` | All application data | Yes |
| `minecraft-network-manager_redis-data` | Rate-limit counters, caches | No (can be lost) |

Also back up your `.env` file (it contains the database credentials and `JWT_SECRET`) and store it securely – it contains secrets.

## Database backup (consistent, online)

```sh
mkdir -p backups
docker compose exec -T mysql sh -c 'exec mysqldump --single-transaction --routines --triggers --no-tablespaces -u root -p"$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"' \
  | gzip > "backups/mnm-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).sql.gz"
```

`--single-transaction` produces a consistent snapshot without locking InnoDB tables. Backups contain personal data (e.g. IP addresses): store them encrypted and restrict access. Example retention (keep 14 days):

```sh
find backups -name 'mnm-*.sql.gz' -mtime +14 -delete
```

Schedule both commands with cron on the host, e.g. daily at 03:30.

## Restore

```sh
docker compose stop backend dashboard
gunzip -c backups/mnm-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sql.gz \
  | docker compose exec -T mysql sh -c 'exec mysql -u root -p"$MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$MYSQL_DATABASE"'
docker compose start backend dashboard
```

Restore into the same application version that created the backup (or older migrations will be re-applied forward on start).

## Disaster recovery

1. Provision a new host, clone the repository at the same version, restore `.env`.
2. `docker compose up -d mysql redis` and wait until healthy.
3. Restore the latest database backup (above).
4. `docker compose up -d`.

Inventory snapshot recovery will be documented with the inventory module (v0.6.0).

```

`docs/installation/deployment.md`:

```md
# Production deployment

This guide takes a fresh Linux host to a production installation. The short version is in the [installation guide](README.md); this page adds the decisions and checks that matter in production.

## 1. Plan

| Topic | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Host | Linux x86_64/arm64, Docker Engine 24+ with Compose, 2 GB RAM (4 GB for large networks), SSD |
| Network | The dashboard must be reachable by staff (browser) **and** by every Minecraft server (plugins). Database and Redis are never exposed. |
| Domain & TLS | A domain such as `admin.example.net` with HTTPS (bundled Caddy profile or your own reverse proxy) |
| Same host as Minecraft? | Possible. Plugins can then use the private address (`http://10.0.0.5:3000`); staff should still use HTTPS. |

## 2. Configure the environment

```sh
git clone <repository-url> minecraft-network-manager
cd minecraft-network-manager
sh infrastructure/scripts/generate-secrets.sh   # creates .env with random secrets
```

### Environment reference (`.env`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MYSQL_DATABASE`, `MYSQL_USER` | `mnm` | Database and user |
| `MYSQL_PASSWORD`, `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD` | – (required) | Database passwords, letters and digits only |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | – (required) | Redis password, letters and digits only |
| `JWT_SECRET` | – (required) | Signs session tokens, ≥ 32 random characters |
| `SETUP_TOKEN` | empty | Fixed setup code (≥ 16 chars); empty = random code in the backend log |
| `DASHBOARD_BIND`, `DASHBOARD_PORT` | `0.0.0.0`, `3000` | Published address of the dashboard. Use `127.0.0.1` behind a reverse proxy on the same host. |
| `COOKIE_SECURE` | `auto` | `true` behind HTTPS |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | private ranges | Proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted ([HTTPS](https.md)) |
| `GEOIP_CITY_DB`, `GEOIP_ASN_DB` | empty | Optional GeoLite2 databases in `./geoip` |
| `API_DOCS_ENABLED` | `true` | OpenAPI docs at `/api/docs` |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `log` | `error`, `warn`, `log`, `debug`, `verbose` |
| `DASHBOARD_DOMAIN`, `ACME_EMAIL` | – | Caddy HTTPS profile |
| `MNM_IMAGE_PREFIX`, `MNM_VERSION` | `mnm`, `latest` | Prebuilt images from a registry instead of local builds |

`.env` contains secrets: keep it out of version control and readable only by the operator (`chmod 600 .env`).

## 3. Start and secure

```sh
docker compose up -d --build                 # or: docker compose --profile https up -d --build
docker compose ps                            # all services healthy
docker compose logs backend | grep "Setup code"
```

- Open the dashboard and run the [setup wizard](README.md#steps). English is preselected; the wizard locks itself after completion.
- Firewall: allow only 80/443 (HTTPS profile) or the dashboard port from the networks that need it. MySQL and Redis have no published ports.
- Set `COOKIE_SECURE=true` once HTTPS works and restart: `docker compose up -d`.

## 4. Configure the network

In the dashboard, as owner:

1. **Settings → General** – network details and the dashboard URL (used as the default backend URL for plugin configurations).
2. **User Management** – invite staff with the least privileged role that fits; review role permissions.
3. **Settings → Minecraft integration** – add the Velocity proxy and every Paper server with the generator ([details](../architecture/configuration.md#adding-a-server-registration-workflow)). Install the plugins as described in [Minecraft plugins](minecraft-plugins.md).
4. **Settings → Plugin settings** – network-wide plugin language, statistics and inventory options, message texts.
5. **Settings → Moderation** – punishment templates; **AntiCheat** – rules (nothing is punished automatically until you add rules).
6. **Settings → Languages / Privacy** – languages offered to staff, IP retention period.

## 5. Operate

- **Backups:** schedule the database and configuration backups with cron and test a restore – see [Backup & restore](backup-restore.md). Plugin data folders (`credentials.properties`, `punishments-cache.json`, `managed-settings.json`) belong into the Minecraft servers' own backups.
- **Updates:** [Updating](updating.md). Database migrations run automatically on start; take a backup first.
- **Monitoring:** `docker compose ps` health states; `GET /api/health/ready` for external monitors; Servers page for plugin heartbeats.
- **Credential hygiene:** rotate a server's credentials on its page when a server is reinstalled or compromised; revoke unused registration tokens.

## Checklist

- [ ] `.env` generated, not committed, `chmod 600`
- [ ] HTTPS active, `COOKIE_SECURE=true`
- [ ] Setup completed, owner password stored in a password manager
- [ ] Only required ports reachable
- [ ] All servers show *Online*; Paper names match `velocity.toml`
- [ ] Backups scheduled and a restore tested

`docs/installation/https.md`:

```md
# HTTPS

## Built-in Caddy (recommended)

1. Point a DNS record (e.g. `admin.example.net`) at the host. Ports 80 and 443 must be reachable.
2. In `.env`:

   ```dotenv
   DASHBOARD_DOMAIN=admin.example.net
   ACME_EMAIL=you@example.net
   DASHBOARD_BIND=127.0.0.1   # stop exposing plain HTTP on :3000
   COOKIE_SECURE=true
   ```

3. Start with the profile:

   ```sh
   docker compose --profile https up -d
   ```

Caddy obtains and renews Let's Encrypt certificates automatically and adds HSTS.

## Your own reverse proxy

Forward all traffic to the dashboard (`:3000`). Requirements:

- Terminate TLS and set `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`.
- **Overwrite** (do not append to) `X-Forwarded-For` with the real client address – the dashboard forwards only the right-most hop to the backend.
- Set `COOKIE_SECURE=true`.

Example (nginx):

```nginx
location / {
  proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000;
  proxy_set_header Host $host;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}
```

```

`docs/installation/minecraft-plugins.md`:

```md
# Installing the Minecraft plugins

| Plugin | Jar | Platform | Java |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Velocity | `NetworkManager-Velocity-<version>.jar` | Velocity 4.3+ | 25 |
| Paper | `NetworkManager-Paper-<version>.jar` | Paper 26.1+ | 25 |

Build them with `./gradlew build` (output in `apps/velocity-plugin/build/libs` and `apps/paper-plugin/build/libs`), or download the `minecraft-plugins` artifact from a CI run.

## 1. Generate the configuration (recommended)

Dashboard → **Settings → Minecraft integration** → *Add a server*:

1. Choose **Velocity** (one per proxy) or **Paper** (one per backend server) and enter the name. **Paper servers must use exactly the server name from `velocity.toml`** (e.g. `lobby`, `survival`), otherwise server switches cannot be linked to the server.
2. Adjust the options (connection, moderation, statistics, inventories, AntiCheat allow-list). The preview shows the resulting `config.properties`.
3. Click **Create token & configuration** and download the ZIP package (configuration + `INSTALL.md`) or `config.properties`.
4. Put the jar into `plugins/`, copy the configuration to `plugins/networkmanager/config.properties` (Velocity) or `plugins/NetworkManager/config.properties` (Paper) and start the server.

The dashboard page shows when the plugin has registered and when the first heartbeat arrived. Tokens are single-use and expire after 30 minutes (`REGISTRATION_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES`). Details: [Configuration management](../architecture/configuration.md).

## 2. Manual configuration (alternative)

1. Put the jar into `plugins/` and start the server once. The plugin creates its `config.properties`.
2. Create a registration token in the same dashboard section and edit `config.properties`:

   ```properties
   backend-url=https://admin.example.net   # dashboard address, no path
   registration-token=mnm_reg_...
   language=en-US
   ```

3. Restart. The log shows `Registered with the backend as "<name>"`. The token is exchanged for credentials stored in `credentials.properties` (keep this file secret; it is created with owner-only permissions where supported). The token can then be removed from the config.

All options are documented in the generated `config.properties`. With `managed-settings=true` (default) the language, plugin messages, statistics and inventory options can be changed centrally under Settings → Plugin settings and apply without a restart; all other options require a restart.

| Option | Default | Platform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `punishments-enabled` | `true` | Both: enforce network bans (proxy) and mutes (Paper) |
| `moderation-commands` | `true` | Velocity: register the in-game moderation commands |
| `managed-settings` | `true` | Both: accept centrally managed plugin settings |

## 3. Verify

- Dashboard → **Servers**: the server appears and switches to *Online* after the first heartbeat (every 15 s by default).
- In game or console: `/networkmanager` (alias `/nm`, permission `networkmanager.admin`) shows the connection status and the number of buffered events.

## What is collected

| Source | Data |
| --- | --- |
| Velocity | join/leave times, server switches, username history, client protocol/version, client brand, virtual host, IP address (disable with `collect-ip-addresses=false`), proxy player count, memory, CPU |
| Paper | TPS, MSPT, player count, memory, CPU, players' game mode, player statistics (see [Statistics](../architecture/statistics.md); configurable or disable with `statistics-enabled=false`) |

Nothing is estimated: values that were not collected are shown as "not collected".

## Moderation

The Velocity plugin provides `/ban`, `/tempban`, `/unban`, `/mute`, `/tempmute`, `/unmute`, `/kick`, `/warn`, `/history` and `/check`. Permissions and behaviour are described in [Punishments](../architecture/punishments.md). Both plugins keep `punishments-cache.json` in their folder so bans and mutes stay enforced during backend outages; do not delete it while the backend is unreachable.

## AntiCheat

Allow-list AntiCheat plugins with `anticheat-integrations=Grim,Vulcan` (Paper `config.properties`) and configure rules in the dashboard. Details: [AntiCheat](../architecture/anticheat.md).

## Inventories

The Paper plugin uploads inventory and Ender Chest snapshots on join, on quit and every `inventory-sync-interval-seconds` (default 300), and applies dashboard edits within a few seconds. Disable with `inventory-sync=false` / `enderchest-sync=false`. Details: [Inventory management](../architecture/inventory.md).

## Outages and restarts

- Player events are buffered in memory (default 50 000) while the backend is unreachable and delivered in order when it returns. If the buffer overflows, the oldest events are dropped and the proxy sends a full **sync** of all connected players, which repairs session state.
- The proxy also syncs every 60 seconds and after every reconnect.
- On a graceful shutdown the plugin delivers pending events and notifies the backend; open sessions are closed.
- If a proxy crashes, the backend closes its sessions after 3 minutes without a heartbeat (end time = last heartbeat).

## Credential management

On a server's detail page in the dashboard:

- **Rotate credentials** – issues a new key and revokes the old one. Replace `credentials.properties` with the displayed values and restart.
- **Revoke credentials** – disconnects the server until it registers again (delete `credentials.properties`, set a new token).
- **Disable** – the backend rejects the server's requests until re-enabled.

## Troubleshooting

| Log message | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Not registered with the backend` | Set `registration-token` and restart |
| `Registration token was rejected` | Token expired or already used – create a new one |
| `The backend rejected this server's credentials` | Credentials were rotated or revoked – see above |
| `PLUGIN_AUTH_CLOCK_SKEW` (backend log) | Server clock differs by more than 5 minutes – enable NTP |
| Server switches show no server | Paper server name in the dashboard differs from `velocity.toml` – rename it on the server's detail page |

`docs/installation/updating.md`:

```md
# Updating

**Always take a backup first** ([Backup & restore](backup-restore.md)). Database migrations are forward-only and cannot be rolled back automatically.

## Using locally built images (default)

```sh
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
```

## Using published images

Once release images are published to GHCR (workflow `release.yml`, triggered by `vX.Y.Z` tags), set in `.env`:

```dotenv
MNM_IMAGE_PREFIX=ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>
MNM_VERSION=0.2.0   # or "latest"
```

Then:

```sh
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

## What happens during an update

1. Containers are recreated; the volumes `mysql-data` and `redis-data` are kept.
2. The backend entrypoint runs `prisma migrate deploy` and applies new migrations before accepting traffic. If a migration fails the backend refuses to start (data is not modified further) – restore the backup or fix the cause, then start again.
3. Startup synchronisation adds new permissions and languages without overwriting customised roles.

To skip automatic migrations (e.g. to run them manually) set `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` on the backend service.

```

#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.

#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/3d91ce3b8caaf77ad09f381f43615b715b53f72c/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac



# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -jar "$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar" \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

```

# HTTPS reverse proxy for the dashboard (enabled with: docker compose --profile https up -d).
# Caddy obtains and renews certificates automatically for DASHBOARD_DOMAIN.
# It replaces client-supplied X-Forwarded-For headers, so the backend sees real client IPs.
{
	email {$ACME_EMAIL}
}

{$DASHBOARD_DOMAIN} {
	encode zstd gzip
	header {
		Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
		-Server
	}
	reverse_proxy dashboard:3000
}

`infrastructure/docker/backend-entrypoint.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Applies pending database migrations, then starts the backend.
# Migrations are forward-only; take a backup before upgrading (docs/installation/backup-restore.md).
set -eu

if [ "${RUN_MIGRATIONS:-true}" = "true" ]; then
  echo "[entrypoint] Applying database migrations…"
  attempt=1
  until npx --no-install prisma migrate deploy; do
    if [ "$attempt" -ge "${MIGRATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS:-10}" ]; then
      echo "[entrypoint] Migrations failed after $attempt attempts. Refusing to start." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[entrypoint] Database not ready (attempt $attempt). Retrying in 5s…" >&2
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 5
  done
fi

exec "$@"

```

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Backend API (NestJS). Build context: repository root.

ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:22-bookworm-slim

# ── Base: matching npm major (lockfile + allowScripts) ───────────────
FROM ${NODE_IMAGE} AS base
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssl ca-certificates tini \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && npm install -g npm@12 --no-audit --no-fund
WORKDIR /app
ENV NPM_CONFIG_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=false

# ── Dependencies (cached on manifest changes only) ───────────────────
FROM base AS deps
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
COPY packages/shared-types/package.json packages/shared-types/
COPY packages/translations/package.json packages/translations/
COPY apps/backend/package.json apps/backend/
RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --workspace @mnm/backend --workspace @mnm/shared-types --workspace @mnm/translations --include-workspace-root

# ── Build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM deps AS build
COPY tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/shared-types packages/shared-types
COPY packages/translations packages/translations
COPY apps/backend apps/backend
RUN npm run build -w @mnm/shared-types -w @mnm/translations \
 && npm run build -w @mnm/backend \
 && npm prune --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund --workspace @mnm/backend --workspace @mnm/shared-types --workspace @mnm/translations --include-workspace-root

# ── Runtime ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM base AS runtime
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT=4000
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/package.json ./package.json
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/shared-types/package.json /app/packages/shared-types/package.json
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/shared-types/dist /app/packages/shared-types/dist
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/translations/package.json /app/packages/translations/package.json
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/translations/dist /app/packages/translations/dist
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/translations/locales /app/packages/translations/locales
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/packages/translations/minecraft /app/packages/translations/minecraft
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/backend/package.json /app/apps/backend/package.json
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/backend/dist /app/apps/backend/dist
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/backend/prisma /app/apps/backend/prisma
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/backend/prisma.config.ts /app/apps/backend/prisma.config.ts
COPY --chown=node:node infrastructure/docker/backend-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/backend-entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/backend-entrypoint.sh

WORKDIR /app/apps/backend
USER node
EXPOSE 4000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=5 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+(process.env.PORT||4000)+'/api/health/ready').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"

CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

`infrastructure/scripts/generate-secrets.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Creates .env from .env.example with freshly generated secrets.
# Requires: openssl (or run inside Docker: docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/w" -w /w alpine/openssl ...).
set -eu

cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."

if [ -f .env ]; then
  echo ".env already exists – refusing to overwrite it." >&2
  exit 1
fi

hex() { openssl rand -hex "$1"; }

sed \
  -e "s/^MYSQL_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME$/MYSQL_PASSWORD=$(hex 24)/" \
  -e "s/^MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME$/MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD=$(hex 24)/" \
  -e "s/^REDIS_PASSWORD=CHANGE_ME$/REDIS_PASSWORD=$(hex 24)/" \
  -e "s/^JWT_SECRET=CHANGE_ME$/JWT_SECRET=$(hex 48)/" \
  .env.example > .env
chmod 600 .env

echo "Created .env with generated secrets. Review it, then run: docker compose up -d"

```

export const DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en-US' as const;

/** Locales shipped with the platform. Additional locales can be registered at runtime. */
export const BUNDLED_LOCALES = ['en-US', 'de-DE'] as const;
export type BundledLocale = (typeof BUNDLED_LOCALES)[number];

/** BCP 47 tag of form ll-RR, e.g. en-US. Used to validate user-supplied locale codes. */
export const LOCALE_PATTERN = /^[a-z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2}$/;

export function isValidLocaleCode(value: string): boolean {
  return LOCALE_PATTERN.test(value);
}

`packages/shared-types/src/permissions.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Canonical permission catalogue. Backend authorization is the source of truth;
 * the dashboard uses these keys only to hide UI it would be refused anyway.
 */
export const PERMISSIONS = {
  PLAYERS_VIEW: 'players.view',
  PLAYERS_VIEW_IP: 'players.view.ip',
  PLAYERS_VIEW_LOCATION: 'players.view.location',
  PLAYERS_VIEW_INVENTORY: 'players.view.inventory',
  PLAYERS_EDIT_INVENTORY: 'players.edit.inventory',
  PLAYERS_VIEW_STATISTICS: 'players.view.statistics',
  PLAYERS_NOTES: 'players.notes',

  PUNISHMENTS_BAN: 'punishments.ban',
  PUNISHMENTS_UNBAN: 'punishments.unban',
  PUNISHMENTS_MUTE: 'punishments.mute',
  PUNISHMENTS_UNMUTE: 'punishments.unmute',
  PUNISHMENTS_KICK: 'punishments.kick',
  PUNISHMENTS_WARN: 'punishments.warn',
  PUNISHMENTS_BLACKLIST: 'punishments.blacklist',
  PUNISHMENTS_HISTORY: 'punishments.history',

  ANTICHEAT_VIEW: 'anticheat.view',
  ANTICHEAT_MANAGE: 'anticheat.manage',

  SERVERS_VIEW: 'servers.view',
  SERVERS_MANAGE: 'servers.manage',

  DASHBOARD_MANAGE: 'dashboard.manage',
  USERS_VIEW: 'users.view',
  USERS_MANAGE: 'users.manage',
  ROLES_MANAGE: 'roles.manage',
  SETTINGS_MANAGE: 'settings.manage',
  TRANSLATIONS_MANAGE: 'translations.manage',
  AUDIT_VIEW: 'audit.view',
} as const;

export type Permission = (typeof PERMISSIONS)[keyof typeof PERMISSIONS];

export const ALL_PERMISSIONS: readonly Permission[] = Object.values(PERMISSIONS);

/** Wildcard granted to the Owner role; matches every permission. */
export const WILDCARD_PERMISSION = '*';

export function isKnownPermission(value: string): value is Permission {
  return (ALL_PERMISSIONS as readonly string[]).includes(value);
}

/**
 * Returns true when the granted set satisfies the required permission.
 * Supports the global wildcard ("*") and namespace wildcards ("players.*").
 */
export function hasPermission(granted: Iterable<string>, required: string): boolean {
  for (const g of granted) {
    if (g === WILDCARD_PERMISSION || g === required) return true;
    if (g.endsWith('.*') && required.startsWith(g.slice(0, -1))) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

`packages/shared-types/src/stats.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Statistic keys reported by the Paper plugin.
 *
 * - `custom:<namespaced key>`  vanilla untyped statistics (e.g. custom:minecraft:jump)
 * - `mined:` / `placed:` / `killed:` + namespaced id  per block / entity type
 * - `mnm:*`  values tracked by the plugin itself (AFK time, chat, XP) or totals
 *
 * Values are cumulative per server. A missing value means "never collected".
 */
export type StatCategory = 'movement' | 'combat' | 'blocks' | 'general';
/** cm: distance in centimetres; damage: tenths of a heart; ticks: 1/20 s. */
export type StatUnit = 'count' | 'cm' | 'damage' | 'ticks' | 'seconds';

export const STATS = {
  WALK: 'custom:minecraft:walk_one_cm',
  SPRINT: 'custom:minecraft:sprint_one_cm',

  FLY: 'custom:minecraft:fly_one_cm',
  ELYTRA: 'custom:minecraft:aviate_one_cm',
  BOAT: 'custom:minecraft:boat_one_cm',

`packages/translations/scripts/validate.mjs`:

```mjs
// Validates every bundled translation catalogue against the en-US reference.
// Fails (exit 1) on unsafe content, structural errors or unknown keys.
// Missing keys are reported as warnings because English is used as fallback.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const root = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const { validateCatalog, findMissingKeys, findUnknownKeys, DEFAULT_LOCALE } = require(join(root, 'dist', 'src', 'index.js'));

const localesDir = join(root, 'locales');
const reference = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(localesDir, `${DEFAULT_LOCALE}.json`), 'utf8'));
let failed = false;

for (const file of readdirSync(localesDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))) {
  const locale = file.replace(/\.json$/, '');
  const catalog = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(localesDir, file), 'utf8'));
  const issues = validateCatalog(catalog);
  for (const issue of issues) console.error(`✖ ${locale}: ${issue.key} → ${issue.problem}`);
  if (issues.length) failed = true;

  if (catalog?.meta?.locale !== locale) {
    console.error(`✖ ${locale}: meta.locale must equal the file name`);
    failed = true;
  }
  const unknown = findUnknownKeys(reference, catalog);
  for (const key of unknown) console.error(`✖ ${locale}: unknown key ${key}`);
  if (unknown.length) failed = true;

  const missing = findMissingKeys(reference, catalog);
  for (const key of missing) console.warn(`⚠ ${locale}: missing key ${key} (falls back to ${DEFAULT_LOCALE})`);
  console.log(`${locale}: ${issues.length + unknown.length} error(s), ${missing.length} missing key(s)`);
}

// Minecraft plugin message files: every locale must define the same keys as en-US.
const mcDir = join(root, 'minecraft');
const keysOf = (text) =>
  text
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((l) => l.match(/^([a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)*):\s*"/)?.[1])
    .filter(Boolean);
const mcReference = new Set(keysOf(readFileSync(join(mcDir, `${DEFAULT_LOCALE}.yml`), 'utf8')));
for (const file of readdirSync(mcDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.yml'))) {
  const text = readFileSync(join(mcDir, file), 'utf8');
  const keys = new Set(keysOf(text));
  const unknown = [...keys].filter((k) => !mcReference.has(k));
  for (const k of unknown) console.error(`✖ minecraft/${file}: unknown key ${k}`);
  if (unknown.length) failed = true;
  const missing = [...mcReference].filter((k) => !keys.has(k));
  for (const k of missing) console.warn(`⚠ minecraft/${file}: missing key ${k}`);
  console.log(`minecraft/${file}: ${keys.size} keys`);
}

if (failed) {
  console.error('Translation validation failed.');
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('All translation catalogues are valid.');

```

`packages/translations/src/index.ts`:

```ts
import enUS from '../locales/en-US.json';
import deDE from '../locales/de-DE.json';

export type MessageTree = { [key: string]: string | MessageTree };

export const DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en-US';

/** Catalogues bundled with the platform, keyed by BCP 47 locale code. */
export const bundledCatalogs: Readonly<Record<string, MessageTree>> = {
  'en-US': enUS as MessageTree,
  'de-DE': deDE as MessageTree,
};

export function getBundledLocales(): string[] {
  return Object.keys(bundledCatalogs);
}

/** Flattens a nested catalogue into dot-separated keys. */
export function flattenMessages(tree: MessageTree, prefix = ''): Record<string, string> {
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(tree)) {
    const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
    if (typeof value === 'string') out[path] = value;
    else Object.assign(out, flattenMessages(value, path));
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Deep-merges `overrides` on top of `base`. Used to fall back to English for
 * keys missing in another locale.
 */
export function mergeWithFallback(base: MessageTree, overrides: MessageTree | undefined): MessageTree {
  if (!overrides) return base;
  const result: MessageTree = { ...base };
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(overrides)) {
    const baseValue = base[key];
    if (typeof value === 'string') {
      if (baseValue === undefined || typeof baseValue === 'string') result[key] = value;
    } else if (baseValue !== undefined && typeof baseValue !== 'string') {
      result[key] = mergeWithFallback(baseValue, value);
    }
  }
  return result;
}

/** Returns the catalogue for `locale` with English used for any missing keys. */
export function getMessages(locale: string): MessageTree {
  const base = bundledCatalogs[DEFAULT_LOCALE];
  if (locale === DEFAULT_LOCALE) return base;
  return mergeWithFallback(base, bundledCatalogs[locale]);
}

/** Keys present in the reference catalogue but missing from `candidate`. */
export function findMissingKeys(reference: MessageTree, candidate: MessageTree): string[] {
  const have = flattenMessages(candidate);
  return Object.keys(flattenMessages(reference)).filter((k) => !(k in have));
}

/** Keys present in `candidate` that do not exist in the reference catalogue. */
export function findUnknownKeys(reference: MessageTree, candidate: MessageTree): string[] {
  const ref = flattenMessages(reference);
  return Object.keys(flattenMessages(candidate)).filter((k) => !(k in ref));
}

// Markup is never allowed in translations: catalogues are rendered as text and
// may originate from untrusted imports.
const FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS: readonly RegExp[] = [/<[a-z!/?]/i, /javascript:/i, /on[a-z]+\s*=/i, /&#/];

export interface ValidationIssue {
  key: string;
  problem: 'not-a-string' | 'unsafe-content' | 'unbalanced-braces' | 'invalid-key' | 'too-long';
}

const KEY_SEGMENT = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/;
const MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2000;

/** Structural and safety validation for an (untrusted) translation catalogue. */
export function validateCatalog(input: unknown, prefix = ''): ValidationIssue[] {
  const issues: ValidationIssue[] = [];
  if (typeof input !== 'object' || input === null || Array.isArray(input)) {
    return [{ key: prefix || '<root>', problem: 'not-a-string' }];
  }
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(input as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
    if (!KEY_SEGMENT.test(key)) {
      issues.push({ key: path, problem: 'invalid-key' });
      continue;
    }
    if (typeof value === 'string') {
      if (value.length > MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH) issues.push({ key: path, problem: 'too-long' });
      if (FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(value))) issues.push({ key: path, problem: 'unsafe-content' });
      if (!bracesBalanced(value)) issues.push({ key: path, problem: 'unbalanced-braces' });
    } else if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)) {
      issues.push(...validateCatalog(value, path));
    } else {
      issues.push({ key: path, problem: 'not-a-string' });
    }
  }
  return issues;
}

function bracesBalanced(value: string): boolean {
  let depth = 0;
  for (const ch of value) {
    if (ch === '{') depth++;
    else if (ch === '}') depth--;
    if (depth < 0) return false;
  }
  return depth === 0;
}

/**
 * Parses a Minecraft plugin message catalogue (`minecraft/<locale>.yml`). The
 * files use a flat subset of YAML: `key: "double-quoted value"` per line plus
 * comments, so no YAML library is needed.
 */
export function parseMinecraftCatalog(text: string): Record<string, string> {
  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const match = /^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*):\s*(".*")\s*$/.exec(line);
    if (!match) continue;
    out[match[1]] = JSON.parse(match[2]) as string;
  }
  return out;
}

/** `{name}` placeholders used in a plugin message. */
export function messagePlaceholders(text: string): string[] {
  return [...new Set([...text.matchAll(/\{([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)\}/g)].map((m) => m[1]))];
}
